recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Revisit only if OO creates a new tracker to make DeviceRequest.performer repeatable or to add request-performerOrder support despite the current singular cardinality.
issue_request: FHIR-26953 was Published with resolution Persuasive with Modification. The original request asked to make request-performerOrder usable for DeviceRequest when multiple performers are listed, but the accepted resolution was to change DeviceRequest.performer to a CodeableReference and drop DeviceRequest.performerType.
initial_application: Explicit source commits 25cc0f276f and f8644c49e8 applied FHIR-26953 by changing DeviceRequest.performer from Reference to CodeableReference and removing DeviceRequest.performerType from the live element list. Later cleanup commit f8afeaa14a removed the commented-out performerType block.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini marks DeviceRequest active in the current build and records the old DeviceRequest.performerType as mapped to performer.concept for the R5 transition. The FHIR Extension Pack request-performerOrder definition applies to ServiceRequest.performer and Task.requestedPerformer, not DeviceRequest.performer. Because current DeviceRequest.performer remains 0..1, adding performerOrder to DeviceRequest would go beyond the final Jira resolution. Community searches found no Zulip conflict; Confluence OO/HCP agenda/minutes references tracked checking PAO impact for the CodeableReference change.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit because the active DeviceRequest source already has performer as a singular CodeableReference and has no live performerType element.
